questions.q: Two objects <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo> </mo><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mo> </mo><mi>B</mi></math> are placed at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><mi>and</mi><mo> </mo><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the pole in front of a concave mirror having radius of curvature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The distance between images formed by the mirror is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let's consider the following diagram-

Let's assume that vA, vB indicates the distances of the images of objects A and B respectively.

Thus, by mirror formula, for object A, it can be written that

1v+1u=1f1vA+1-15=1-201vA=1-20+115=-3+460vA=60 cm

Similarly, for object B, using mirror formula,

1vB+1-25=1-201vB=-120+125=-5+4100=-1100vB=-100 cm

Hence, the distance d between the images can be calculated as follows:

d= vA+vB= 60+100 cm= 160 cm

questions.q: Light travels in two media <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> with speeds <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> respectively. The critical angle between them is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Relative refractive index can be found as,

μ2μ1=v1v2=1.52=34.

When the angle of incident is greater than the critical angle total internal reflection occurs. If the critical angle is ic then,

sinic=μ2μ1=34

Now tanic=342-32=37

Therefore, ic=tan-137

Optical path length =OA+μOB
=acos 60o+μbcos 30o
=2a+μ2b3
From Snell’s law,
sin 60o=μ sin 30o
μ=3
Optical path length =2a+32b3

questions.q: The thickness at the centre of a plano convex lens is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and the diameter is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math> If the speed of light in the material of the lens is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> The focal length of the lens is ___________.
questions.subject: Physics

R2=r2+(R-t)2

Neglecting t2, we get

R=r22t

∴1f=μ-11R-1∞=μ-1R

f=Rμ-1=r22t(μ-1)=3×10-222×3×10-3×32-1

=9×10-46×10-3×1×2

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R)
Assertion (A) : Refractive index of glass is higher than that of air.
Reason ( $\mathrm{R}$) : Optical density of a medium is directly proportionate to its mass density which results in a proportionate refractive index.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: $(\mathrm{A})$ is not correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is correct
Both $(\mathrm{A})$ and $(\mathrm{R})$ are correct and $(\mathrm{R})$ is the correct explanation of (A)
$(A)$ is correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Refractive index has no relation with mass density because both have different meaning. Hence reason is incorrect.
So (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

questions.q: In normal adjustment, for a refracting telescope, the distance between objective and eye piece is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The focal length of the objective, when the angular magnification of the telescope is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math>, will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let f0 be the focal length of objective and fe is the focal length of eyepiece.

Given here, f0+fe=30.

Angular magnification of telescope is given by m=f0fe.

So, 2=f0fe⇒f0=2fe

Then, we have f0+f02=30⇒3f02=30

Or, f0=20 cm.

questions.q: For the thin convex lens, the radii of curvature are at $15 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $30 \mathrm{~cm}$ respectively. The focal length the lens is $20 \mathrm{~cm}$. The refractive index of the material is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=\left(\frac{\mu_{\text {lens }}}{\mu_{\text {air }}}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_1}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_2}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{+20}=\left(\frac{\mu}{1}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{+15}-\frac{1}{(-30)}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{20}=(\mu-1)\left(\frac{3}{30}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mu-1=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \mu=1+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{2}=1 \cdot 5\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Time taken by light to travel in two different materials <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> of refractive indices <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></math> of same thickness is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> respectively. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> and the ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Then the thickness of material, in meter is: (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></math> are velocities of light in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> materials respectively).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The speed of light in a medium is inversely proportional to the refractive index of the material. Therefore,

μAμB=vBvA=12

Let the thickness is d

⇒t2-t1=dvB-dvA=5×10-10 s

As vA=2vB⇒d=5×10-10×2vB

⇒d=5×10-10×vA m.

questions.q: An object is placed on the principal axis of convex lens of focal length 10 cm as shown. A plane mirror is placed on the other side of lens at a distance of 20 cm. The image produced by the plane mirror is 5 cm inside the mirror. The distance of the object from the lens is ____ cm.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here: Focal length of convex lens, f=10 cm

Now, as seen in figure, image from lens is formed at point I1, whose location is 5 cm from mirror. Thus, I1 is at 15 cm from lens.

Using lens equation, we have

1v-1u=1f

Putting the value, 

115-1-u=110

⇒1u=110-115⇒u=10×1510-15

Thus, object is placed at 30 cm from lens.

questions.q: An object 'O' is placed at a distance of 100 cm in front of a concave mirror of radius of curvature 200 cm as shown in the figure. The object starts moving towards the mirror at a speed 2 cm s-1. The position of the image from the mirror after 10 s will be at _____ cm.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In 10 s, the object will travel distance =2×10=20 cm

After 10 sec, the object will be at distance u=20-100=-80 m.

Focal length of the concave mirror is f=R2=2002=-100 cm

Using mirror formula,

1v+1u=1f

⇒1v=-1100+180⇒v=800020

⇒v=400 cm

Position of image from the mirror is at 400 cm.

questions.q:
A container contains a liquid with refractive index of 1.2 up to a height of 60 cm and another liquid having refractive index 1.6 is added to height H above first liquid. If viewed from above, the apparent shift in the position of bottom of container is 40 cm. The value of H is ______ cm.
(Consider liquids are immisible)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$y=$ apparent depth of bottom
$\frac{\mathrm{y}}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{H}}{1.6}+\frac{60}{1.2}$
Shift $=40$
$H+60-y=40$
$\mathrm{H}+60-\frac{\mathrm{H}}{1.6}-\frac{60}{1.2}=40$
$\frac{6}{16} \mathrm{H}=30$
$\mathrm{H}=80 \mathrm{~cm}$
